title: Self-Employment Taxes
description: Both halves of FICA, a Schedule C, and the 2026 mileage rates that split in July.
wolfLine: No employer is paying the other half. That half is still due.

self-employment-tax.definition: The Social Security and Medicare tax a self-employed person pays on net earnings. The common case is 15.3% of 92.35% of the net, which is both the employee half and the employer half.
self-employment-tax.example: A $10,000 self-employment base is taxed at 15.3%, which is $1,530.

lessons.title: Both Halves of FICA
lessons.summary: An employee pays one half. You pay both.

steps.title: The common case
steps.body:
[[Self-employment tax]] is both halves of [[FICA]]. In the common case, under the Social Security wage base, it is **15.3%** of **92.35%** of net self-employment earnings.

On a **$20,000** net, the base is **$18,470**. On a round **$10,000** base, 15.3% is **$1,530**. An employee’s half of FICA on $10,000 of wages is **7.65%**, or **$765**. The extra 0.9% Medicare tax is a high-income exception. This lesson does not grade that threshold.

steps.prompt: Net self-employment earnings are $20,000. What is 92.35% of that?
The self-employment base in front of you is $10,000. What is 15.3% of it?
What is the employee half, 7.65%, on $10,000 of wages?
How much more is the $1,530 self-employment tax than that employee half?
steps.explain: $1,530 − $765 = $765. That gap is the employer half, which a self-employed person also pays.

lessons.title: A Schedule C
lessons.summary: Profit is receipts minus the costs you can deduct.

steps.title: The bottom line
steps.body:
Schedule C is the high-level picture of one business. Gross receipts are **$40,000**. Supplies are **$2,000**. Contract help is **$3,000**. Net profit is **$35,000**.

A personal grocery trip is not a line here. A [[business expense]] has to belong to the work.

steps.prompt: What is the net profit on this page?
Supplies and contract help together are how much?
Which cost belongs on this Schedule C?
choices: Software you bought only for client work
A vacation that included one work email
steps.explain: The software is a business expense. The groceries and the vacation are personal.

steps.prompt: Net profit is the gross receipts, with no costs taken off.
steps.explain: Net profit is what remains. Here that is $35,000, not $40,000.

lessons.title: Expenses and a Home Office
lessons.summary: The space has to be for the work, regularly and only.

steps.title: Exclusive means exclusive
steps.body:
Ordinary [[business expense]] items, like the supplies on the Schedule C, come off the receipts.

A home office usually has to be used regularly and only for the business. A desk in the living room, or a spare room that is also the guest room, usually fails that test. This lesson does not assign a dollar deduction for the room. The IRS page for the year is the method, simplified or actual.

steps.prompt: Which space usually qualifies?
choices: A room used only for the business, regularly
The kitchen table, also used for dinner
A guest room with a laptop in the corner
steps.explain: Only, and regularly. Shared family space usually does not qualify.

steps.prompt: A personal grocery bill becomes a business expense because you thought about work while shopping.
steps.explain: The cost has to be for the business. Thinking about work does not convert a personal bill.

steps.prompt: Gross receipts are $35,000. A real business expense is $5,000. What is left before any home-office method?
steps.explain: $35,000 − $5,000 = $30,000. The home office is a separate question, not an automatic extra.

steps.prompt: A home office usually must be used regularly and ___ for the business.
steps.explain: Only. A mixed-use room usually stays personal.

lessons.title: Mileage in 2026
lessons.summary: The rate changed on July 1. Use the half you drove.

steps.title: Two rates, one year
steps.body:
For 2026, the business standard mileage rate is **72.5 cents** a mile from January through June, and **76 cents** from July through December.

It is for business miles of a self-employed person, not for an employee’s commute to a regular workplace. **1,000** miles in the second half are **$760**. The same 1,000 miles in the first half are **$725**. Both halves are **$1,485**. Do not use one rate for the whole year.

steps.prompt: What is 1,000 business miles in July through December 2026, at 76 cents?
What is 1,000 business miles in January through June 2026, at 72.5 cents?
You drove 1,000 business miles in each half. What is the deduction?
The drive from home to a regular W-2 office is a business mile at these rates.
steps.explain: These rates are the self-employed business deduction. A commute to your job is personal.

lessons.title: Quarterly Estimates
lessons.summary: A safe harbor is a target, not a guess.

steps.title: Match last year, or come close to this one
steps.body:
[[Estimated taxes]] are how you pay during the year when no employer is withholding. You already know the quarterly dates.

A common safe harbor is **100%** of last year’s tax, or **110%** if your adjusted gross income was over **$150,000**. Another path is **90%** of this year’s tax. Last year’s tax of **$4,000** makes the 100% target **$4,000**, or **$1,000** a quarter. The 110% target is **$4,400**, or **$1,100** a quarter.

steps.prompt: Last year’s tax was $4,000. What is 100% of it?
steps.explain: The common safe harbor is the whole $4,000.

steps.prompt: Split that $4,000 into four equal quarterly payments. What is each one?
Your adjusted gross income was over $150,000, so you use 110% of the $4,000. What is the target?
The quarterly dates replace the need to pay.
steps.explain: The dates are when the estimates are due. A safe harbor is how much. You already learned the dates.

steps.title: The file is the deduction
steps.body:
Keep the invoice, the receipt, and a mileage log written at the time. A number you reconstruct in April is a weak record.

Personal bills do not go in the business folder just because the folder is nearby.

steps.prompt: Sort each paper.
items: An invoice you sent a client
A log of miles driven to that client
A receipt for software used only for the work
steps.explain: Client income, client miles, and work software stay. The streaming bill is personal.

steps.prompt: When should the mileage log be written?
steps.explain: A log from the day is a record. A log from memory is a story.

steps.prompt: A personal streaming bill is a business expense if it is in the same drawer as the invoices.
steps.explain: The drawer does not change what the bill paid for.

steps.prompt: Write the mileage down when you ___ it.
steps.explain: Drive. April is too late to invent the log.

lessons.title: Rosa’s Second Year
lessons.summary: The base, the miles, and a harbor she can name.

story.title: Rosa’s second year
story.body:
Rosa is 38 and a freelance designer. Her second year’s net profit, before the mileage, is **$20,000**. The self-employment base is 92.35% of that, which is **$18,470**.

She also drove **1,000** miles to clients in July through December 2026. At **76 cents**, that deduction is **$760**. She does not use the January rate for those miles.

She already knows the quarterly dates. Last year’s tax was **$4,000**, and her income was under **$150,000**, so her 100% safe harbor is **$4,000**. She keeps the invoices and the mileage log as she goes.

steps.prompt: What is 92.35% of Rosa’s $20,000 net?
What is her mileage deduction for those 1,000 second-half miles?
What is her 100% safe-harbor target?
steps.explain: 100% of last year’s $4,000 tax is $4,000.

steps.prompt: What is each of four equal payments toward that $4,000?
Rosa should use 72.5 cents for the miles she drove in November.
steps.explain: November is in the second half of 2026. Those miles are 76 cents.

lessons.title: Den Trial: Self-Employment Taxes
lessons.summary: 8 questions. Three strikes and you’re out.

steps.prompt: Net self-employment earnings are $10,000. What is 92.35% of that?
A $8,000 self-employment base is taxed at 15.3%. What is the tax?
Which miles use the 76-cent rate in 2026?
choices: Business miles driven from July through December
The commute to a W-2 job
steps.explain: July through December is the 76-cent half. January is 72.5 cents. The commute is not this deduction.

steps.prompt: A guest room that relatives still sleep in is a clean home office.
steps.explain: The space usually has to be used only for the business.
